You will compare one known error in a data agent's work against a ranked list of items produced by a reviewer. Your job is to decide whether any item in the list identifies this known error, and if so, which one.

An item identifies the known error only if both of these hold:
- It is about the same thing: the same table, and the same column, computation, filter, or join.
- It points to the same problem: what the item says is wrong, assumed, or missing is the same as what went wrong in the known error. It does not matter whether the item is phrased as an assumption the agent made ("the agent assumes ...") or as a problem in the work ("this does not match ..."); judge by meaning.

An item does not count if it only says that something may be wrong without saying what, such as "this column may be computed incorrectly". An item about the same column but a different problem does not count.

If more than one item identifies the error, report the highest-ranked one. If you are unsure, say so rather than guessing.

Return a JSON object with:
- "verdict": "match", "no_match", or "unsure".
- "rank": the position of the matching item (1 is the top), or null.
- "quote": the exact words from the matching item that show it identifies the error, or null.
- "reason": one short sentence.

=== Known error ===
Table: asana__project_analytics
What the agent's work assumed: time_management_score 按完成比例和剩余天数打分就行
What was actually required or true: 按 schedule_forecast 各档映射 25、20、15、10、5，其余 12

=== Reviewer's ranked list for this table ===
[
  {
    "rank": 1,
    "item": {
      "statement": "Time-management scoring may be based on completion and deadline status instead of schedule_forecast.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "target": "marts.asana__project_analytics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "CASE WHEN completion_percentage=100 THEN 25 WHEN remaining_days<0 THEN 5 ELSE 12 END time_management_score",
      "alternative": "The contract maps schedule_forecast to scores: 'on_schedule 25; slight_delay 20; moderate_delay 15; significant_delay 10; overdue 5; else 12'.",
      "reason": "This substitution changes the time score, comprehensive score, and performance ranks.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c7-6",
      "call": 7
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 2,
    "item": {
      "statement": "No project entering project analytics has a negative elapsed_days value.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "marts.asana__project_analytics",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "ROUND(completion_percentage/NULLIF(elapsed_days,0),4) completion_rate_per_day",
      "alternative": "The contract requires completion_rate_per_day to be NULL 'if elapsed_days is not positive', whereas NULLIF only handles zero.",
      "reason": "Future-created projects would receive negative completion rates instead of NULL.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c7-7",
      "call": 7
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 3,
    "item": {
      "statement": "Every non-null project team_id has a matching staged team.",
      "about": "data",
      "target": "marts.asana__project_analytics.team_id",
      "evidence_of_dependence": "SELECT p.project_id,p.project_name,p.team_id,t.team_name",
      "alternative": "The analytics column description says team_id is 'null if no matching team'; selecting p.team_id preserves unmatched identifiers.",
      "reason": "Unmatched teams would leave non-null team identifiers where the output contract calls for NULL.",
      "updates": null,
      "id": "c7-8",
      "call": 7
    }
  }
]
